authors: Burkhard O.; Becker H.; Weibel R.; Axhausen K. W.
title: On the requirements on spatial accuracy and sampling rate for transport mode detection in view of a shift to passive signalling data
measured_object: Transport mode detection from a longitudinal sample of 138 users with GNSS points and mode labels
study_design_and_finding: Compares existing pointwise and segmentwise detection schemes as spatial accuracy and temporal granularity deteriorate; requirements vary by classification scheme and whether whole trajectories are available
error_or_sampling_definition: Sampling interval and spatial accuracy are varied in that study; its settings and quality measures are specific to its data and classifiers
support_for_this_project: Motivates paired evaluation of sampling sparsity and position degradation and comparison of fixed detection pipelines
transfer_limit: It already investigates both quality dimensions and compares detection schemes; do not claim novelty from merely combining the axes or transfer its thresholds to GeoLife 120 s windows

authors: Wang Y.; Yang F.; Li R.; Zhou T.
title: Influence of Location Frequency on Travel Mode Extraction Using Cellular Phone Data
measured_object: Real cellular phone signaling locations paired with observed travel information
study_design_and_finding: Tests a random forest travel mode extractor on resampled cellular data; mode sensitivity to location frequency differs; reports 79.2% overall accuracy in its four-mode task
error_or_sampling_definition: Reported location frequency is average seconds per cellular observation; the study examines much coarser intervals than the GeoLife 5 s and 10 s time buckets
support_for_this_project: Supports the practical motivation that less frequent positioning can affect travel mode recognition differently by class
transfer_limit: Cellular signaling positions and trip or multi-minute features differ from GPS points and 120 s windows; its 60 s per observation recommendation and accuracy cannot be reused as our thresholds

authors: Weng D.; Hou Z.; Meng Y.; Cai M.; Chan Y.
title: Characterization and mitigation of urban GNSS multipath effects on smartphones
measured_object: Smartphone GNSS code measurements in a Hong Kong urban setting
study_design_and_finding: Finds NLOS signals dominate code outliers and tests sidewalk identification to improve urban positioning
error_or_sampling_definition: Reports GNSS ranging and positioning outcomes; its stated accuracy values are not independent x/y Gaussian standard deviations
support_for_this_project: Supports the background that urban obstruction and reflections can degrade smartphone positioning
transfer_limit: Does not calibrate our added independent Gaussian x/y noise; 5/10/20 m sigma levels are synthetic stress settings rather than measured urban canyon categories
